# Stickman presenter — Style Prompt

> A character explainer on warm paper: a big round-headed presenter sits cropped at the bottom right and talks, while anonymous stickmen on a bare left stage act the idea out as causal slapstick with oversized props (a falling coin, a leaking wallet, a toppling tower). Dark ink, restrained red, huge condensed uppercase titles at the top left with a hand-drawn red underline, and captions in the right column that reveal the spoken phrase word by word, upcoming words in grey and the keyword boxed in red.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

A **presenter plus a stage**: two layers with separate jobs. The presenter carries the voice: a mouth that moves with speech and one semantic hand gesture on each important phrase, nothing else. The stage carries the meaning: a nameless stickman whose physical state changes because of a prop (pressed down, dragged, flattened, buried, relieved), with anticipation, contact, consequence and recovery, so a muted viewer still understands. It suits lessons and tips, a creator's opinion, a coach or teacher explaining a habit, a shop explaining why its product helps.

Not a talking head (the presenter is a drawn character, never a photo), not motion-graphics icons (props act on the body, they don't just pop in), not a slideshow (the stage never idles more than about a second without a reason), not a meme collage (one stage, one actor, one gag per idea).

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Paper**: the background, flat and warm, with one thin ground line (ink mixed ~45 % into the paper, 3 px) across the stage at ~91 % of the height.
- **Stage actors**: plain round heads (r ≈ 32 at figure scale 1.3, paper-filled, 5 px ink), two dot eyes, brows and a small mouth; single-line torso and limbs ~5.5 px, round ends for hands, flat ovals for feet. About 6 heads tall. Pose-to-pose with fixed limb lengths; a whole-body squash (to ~16 % height, 160 % width) only when a prop lands on them.
- **Props**: oversized, flat paper-tone fill (`--latar-2`) with 5 px ink outlines; red only as an accent band or a fill level. Coins with "Rp", a wallet, coffee cups with red sleeves, a savings jar whose red fill rises.
- **Presenter**: a large circle head (r ≈ 172 at 1080 high) filled with the main colour, 8 px ink outline, a soft highlight arc, big angled white eyes outlined in ink, a dark mouth with a tongue that opens with speech; neck and shoulders as 8 px ink lines leaving the bottom edge; compact gloves in the main colour (fist, open palm, pointing finger), arms as ink curves from the shoulder.
- **Titles**: plain type over paper with a hand-drawn red underline that draws itself; no boxes or panels.

## 3. Colour logic

- `--latar` is the paper; `--teks` all ink: actors, outlines, titles, spoken words; `--teks-redup` the words not yet spoken and the contact line.
- `--utama` is the presenter (head, gloves), the keyword box (with `--teks-di-utama`), cup sleeves and the jar's fill. `--utama-di-latar` colours the red title words and the underline.
- `--latar-2` fills every prop. `--aksen` is unused by default; keep it for one prop at most.
- Fixed: `--putih` (the presenter's eyes) and `--tanah` (the ground line).
- Rule: the frame is mostly paper and ink; red appears on the presenter, one title word or line, one keyword and one prop detail.

## 4. Type

- `--font-judul` carries the titles: a condensed heavy grotesk in uppercase (Oswald 700 by default; Bebas Neue or Archivo Black suit), 120 px at 1080 high with 0.98 line height, top left, one or two lines, the turning word in red. Leave room: a brand face may run wider.
- `--font-isi` carries the captions: a heavy grotesk (Inter 800 by default), 54 px at 1080 high (60 px vertical), up to three semantic lines in the right column above the presenter, left-aligned, 1.32 line height. Every word of the phrase is shown at once in grey; each turns ink as it is spoken; the keyword gets a red box with white text and a 1.12 → 1 settle.
- A contact block under the final title in `--font-isi` 600, 40 px, the name in 800.

## 5. Motion quality

- **Shot length**: 2.2–3.8 s, hard cuts per idea; titles are optional per shot (some shots are stage-only).
- **Stage acting**: setup → anticipation → contact → exaggerated consequence → delayed secondary motion → recovery. Anticipation ~0.15–0.3 s, contact 0.08–0.12 s `power3.out`, follow-through 0.3–0.5 s, recovery `back.out(2–2.6)`. Falling props `power2.in` 0.28–0.45 s; rolling props carry spin (≈ 360° per 1.5 radii travelled). Running cycles at 0.15 s per step.
- **Presenter**: the mouth opens and closes at 0.11 s per half while a phrase plays and rests closed between phrases; one gesture per key phrase: 0.12 s anticipation, 0.12 s attack, 0.25–0.6 s hold, 0.26 s release; fingers open only after the hand has risen a third of the way; the other hand stays down. A 3° nod on the strongest words, a blink every few seconds.
- **Type**: titles rise 24 px and fade in 0.25 s with 0.12 s between lines; the underline draws in 0.45 s `power2.out`; spoken words switch on the beat, never fade.
- **Camera**: locked. No shake except a single short bump on a heavy landing.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Wide locked stage, title top left | the idea and the actor's situation | a money habit; a study problem; a shop owner's busy day |
| Stage-only shot, no title | the consequence is the message | a leak; a mistake getting worse; a chain reaction |
| Red number title over a growing stack | scale of a fact | spending per month; hours lost; customers missed |
| Presenter's open palm toward the stage | "look at this" | introducing a step; the product; a rule |
| Presenter's raised finger | the one thing to remember | a number; a warning; a key tip |
| Final title with a contact block | where to go next | a class schedule; a shop's chat; a channel's next video |

## 7. Native moves

- **The falling weight.** A giant prop drops, the actor catches it, his body compresses, then the prop escapes and drags him into the next beat. *Fits content like:* a salary coin that rolls away; a pile of homework; a heavy order box; a deadline that lands on a creator.
- **The leak that gets worse.** The actor holds something that loses its contents bit by bit; he shakes it and everything spills at once. *Fits content like:* a wallet with small spends; a bucket of attention; a bag of customers; a phone battery.
- **The toppling tower.** Small items stack one by one past his head, wobble and bury him; he pops back flat-then-round. *Fits content like:* daily coffees; unread messages; unpaid invoices; tabs left open.
- **Lift and place.** He strains under a big prop, then throws it into the right container, which shakes and fills in red. *Fits content like:* saving 20% first; putting the phone in a box; filing a tax form; a stock in a warehouse.
- **The settled sign-off.** He leans on the solved prop with a thumbs-up, the title names the offer, the presenter points, all held. *Fits content like:* a finance class; a coaching program; a shop's bundle; "follow for part 2".

## 8. Pitfalls

- Props that just appear next to an idle actor: something must push, pull, press, bury or drag him, and his silhouette must change.
- Stretched limbs or a floating grip: move the actor or the prop; hands touch what they hold.
- A presenter that waves all the time: one gesture per key phrase, then both hands back down.
- Captions that duplicate the title or show only the current word: show the whole phrase in grey, light words as spoken, box one keyword.
- Too much red: one title word, one keyword, the presenter and one prop detail.
- Putting the presenter in the stage's camera or shaking it: the presenter, titles and captions stay still; only the stage acts.
- Drawing the presenter as a real person or a known character: an original round head with its own eyes and colour.

# Stickman presenter: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 2.2, medium 3.0, long 3.8.

## hook

- en: a two-line question title with a red underline; on stage a giant prop hits the actor, squashes him, then escapes; he chases
- id: judul pertanyaan dua baris bergaris merah; di panggung benda raksasa menimpa aktor, menekannya, lalu lolos; ia mengejar

## problem

- en: no title; the actor's prop fails in steps (leaks, slips, breaks), he shakes it and it gets worse; the presenter shows two palms
- id: tanpa judul; benda aktor gagal bertahap (bocor, lepas, rusak), ia mengocoknya dan makin parah; presenter membuka dua telapak

## fact

- en: the number as a red title; small things stack into a tower taller than the actor, topple and flatten him; he springs back
- id: angka jadi judul merah; benda kecil menumpuk lebih tinggi dari aktor, tumbang dan memipihkannya; ia memantul pulih

## step

- en: a short command title; the actor strains, lifts and throws a big prop into its right place, which shakes and fills
- id: judul perintah singkat; aktor bersusah payah mengangkat dan melempar benda besar ke tempatnya, yang berguncang dan terisi

## compare

- en: two actors side by side, one buried under the problem, one relaxed; a red strike through the wrong word in the title
- id: dua aktor berdampingan, satu tertimbun masalah, satu santai; coretan merah pada kata yang salah di judul

## number

- en: a huge red number title, a stack or a filling container on stage showing the amount; the presenter raises one finger
- id: judul angka merah besar, tumpukan atau wadah yang terisi di panggung menunjukkan jumlahnya; presenter mengacungkan satu jari

## proof

- en: the actor tries the fix and it works: the prop that failed now holds; the caption keyword boxed in red
- id: aktor mencoba solusinya dan berhasil: benda yang tadi gagal kini bertahan; kata kunci teks ucapan dalam kotak merah

## offer

- en: the product as an oversized prop the actor leans on or hugs; name title, price as the red word, the presenter's open palm
- id: produk jadi benda raksasa yang dipeluk atau disandari aktor; judul nama, harga sebagai kata merah, telapak terbuka presenter

## cta

- en: the name as a title with contact lines under it, the actor relaxed by the solved prop, the presenter points; held 2 s
- id: nama jadi judul dengan kontak di bawahnya, aktor santai di samping benda yang beres, presenter menunjuk; diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: the first shot's situation resolved, the actor calm, one closing caption with its keyword boxed; held 2 s
- id: situasi adegan pertama terselesaikan, aktor tenang, satu teks penutup dengan kata kunci berkotak; diam 2 detik
